title: Anglo-Ottoman-Austrian squadron under Admiral Napier bombards Sidon
why: Napier's mixed squadron bombarded Sidon on 26 Sept 1840 and the city capitulated within two days, a step toward Ibrahim Pasha's withdrawal from Syria (corrected from 'Egyptian rule ends there').

title: Battle of Beirut ends Egyptian hold on the city
why: Allied squadron action in October 1840 helped end Egyptian rule and reopened Mount Lebanon's politics.

title: Settlement of hills around Beirut begins, Moussaitbeh and Achrafieh
why: Beirut started to spill beyond its walls; the hill districts became the city's residential core.

title: Beirut replaces Acre as seat of the Ottoman province
why: Beirut's rise as administrative centre set it on the path to becoming Lebanon's capital.

title: Grand Serail built in Beirut
why: The Ottoman government house later became the prime minister's seat.

title: Sarcophagus of King Eshmunazar II found at Sidon
why: The Phoenician inscription gave a rare royal text from Sidon; the sarcophagus went to the Louvre.

title: Hadiqat al-Akhbar newspaper begins in Beirut
why: An early Arabic-language newspaper, founded in the city's printing-press era.

title: Sursock House built in Beirut
why: Part of the Achrafieh palace building by the Greek Orthodox Sursock family.

title: Maghrebi Jewish community builds new synagogue in Sidon
why: Maghrebi Jews had moved from the Chouf to Sidon and Beirut after the 1860 violence, bringing citrus growing.

title: Ernest Renan excavates at Tyre and Byblos
why: His Mission de Phénicie of 1860-61 started modern archaeology in Lebanon's coastal cities.

title: Greek Orthodox archbishop's residence moves to Sursock Street, Achrafieh
why: Shows the Christian move into Achrafieh after 1860.

title: Deir el Qamar creates first municipality in Ottoman Arab provinces
why: A municipal council in the former emirate capital, ahead of Ottoman municipal law.

title: Syrian Protestant College founded in Beirut
why: Became the American University of Beirut in 1920.

title: Road links Jounieh and Ghazir
why: Part of the road works that opened the Keserwan coast to trade.

title: AUB Archaeological Museum established
why: One of the oldest university museums in the region.

title: Moussa Sursock completes his palace in Achrafieh
why: A landmark of the Beirut merchant elite.

title: Brummana Friends School opens
why: The Quaker school was founded by Theophilus Waldmeier in the Metn.

title: Saint Joseph University founded in Beirut
why: Jesuit university that became a pillar of francophone education.

title: Thamarat al-Funun newspaper begins in Beirut
why: An early Beirut Arabic newspaper of the 1870s press boom.

title: Lisan al-Hal newspaper begins in Beirut
why: A long-running Beirut daily.

title: Hotel Palmyra opens in Baalbek
why: Early tourism hotel by the Roman ruins.

title: Hotel-Dieu de France founded in Beirut
why: Jesuit-linked hospital that became a major private hospital.

title: Zahrat al-Ihsan school built in Achrafieh
why: Early Orthodox community school.

title: Ottoman excavation of Sidon's royal necropolis begins
why: Treasures including the Alexander Sarcophagus went to Istanbul.

title: Beirut made capital of a vilayet
why: The province included Latakia, Tripoli, Beirut, Acre and Bekaa sanjaks.

title: Jounieh linked by rail to Beirut
why: Coastal road and rail links boosted the Keserwan coast.

title: Saint Peter's Cathedral built in Marjayoun
why: A landmark church of the town.

title: Beirut harbour built by a French company
why: The modern port that Lebanon still relies on.

title: Saint George Maronite Cathedral built in Beirut
why: A downtown landmark.

title: Beirut-Damascus railway completed
why: Narrow-gauge line over Mount Lebanon; spurred summer resorts such as Aley.

title: Saint Stephen's Cathedral built in Batroun
why: Landmark church of the northern coastal town.

title: Kaiser Wilhelm II visits Baalbek
why: The German emperor's tour boosted German excavation of the temples.

title: Railway reaches Baalbek
why: Connection to the DHP line opened the Bekaa to Beirut and Damascus.

title: Railway accident near Aley kills 8
why: Locomotive exploded and the train rolled back down the 7 percent grade.

title: Tripoli clock tower erected for Abdulhamid II's jubilee
why: Built to mark 30 years of the sultan's reign.

title: Universal College founded in Aley
why: Founded by Shebl Khoury.

title: Our Lady of Lebanon shrine at Harissa inaugurated
why: Bronze statue erected 1907; became a national pilgrimage site above Jounieh.

title: Grand Lycee established near Sodeco in Achrafieh
why: French-language secondary school.

title: Sursock villa completed in Beirut
why: Later became the Sursock Museum.

title: Hangings in Beirut and Damascus, Martyrs' Square named
why: Djemal Pasha's executions of nationalists gave the square its name (renamed formally 1931).

title: National Evangelical School founded in Nabatieh
why: An early mixed-community school in the south.

title: Druze rebels besiege French garrison at Rashaya citadel
why: Part of the Great Syrian Revolt; 429 Christian homes were damaged.

title: Church of the Annunciation rebuilt in Achrafieh
why: Rebuilt after downtown demolition.

title: Original Martyrs' memorial (Les Pleureuses) unveiled in Beirut
why: Youssef Hoyek's statue was unveiled on 19 Dec 1930, the twentieth anniversary of the declaration of Greater Lebanon, per Wikipedia (single source); square renamed 1931 (corrected from 'Martyrs' Monument unveiled').

title: Danger Plan for Beirut proposed, never built
why: A garden-city master plan for Beirut under the Mandate.

title: 33-day general strike in Tripoli
why: Demanded reunification with Syria after the French cut support for the nationalists.

title: Tobacco revolt in Bint Jbeil after gendarmes kill three
why: Bint Jbeil produced about 40,000 kg of tobacco a year in 1936.

title: Jafariya School founded in Tyre
why: Founded by Imam Abdul Hussein Sharafeddin; upgraded to secondary in 1946.

title: Musa Dagh Armenians resettled at Anjar
why: Several thousand Armenian refugees settled beside the Umayyad ruins.

title: Roxy cinema opens in Tyre
why: First of a run of cinemas that closed in the 1980s.

title: Haratch elementary school opens in Anjar
why: Funded by the Armenian paper Haratch.

title: Beiteddine named presidential summer residence
why: Part of the Lebanese presidency's summer-seat tradition.

title: Deir el Qamar declared presidential summer residence
why: Wikipedia says President Bechara El Khoury declared it the summer palace for Lebanese presidents in 1943 (flagged citation needed); the town was protected as a monument in 1945 (corrected from 'palace').

title: Independence leaders detained at Rashaya citadel
why: Khoury, Solh and others held until 22 Nov, now Independence Day.

title: Bourj Hammoud becomes an independent municipality
why: The Armenian-majority suburb got its own council.

title: First ski lift installed at the Cedars
why: Government lift opened Lebanon's oldest ski resort.

title: Beirut airport opens
why: Now Rafic Hariri International.

title: Baalbeck International Festival first organised
why: Part of the Touristic Year 1955; first full season followed in 1956.

title: Camille Chamoun Sports City Stadium opens in Beirut
why: Rebuilt in 1997.

title: Upper galleries of Jeita Grotto discovered, lower cave opens
why: George Farra and Sami Karkabi found the upper galleries.

title: Tele Liban begins broadcasting
why: Launch of national television.

title: Casino du Liban opens in Maameltein
why: A symbol of 1960s Lebanese nightlife.

title: Martyrs' Monument by Mazzacurati inaugurated
why: Replaced the original weeping women statue.

title: Beirut Arab University established
why: A private university.

title: Sursock Museum opens
why: Opened under director Amine Beyhum.

title: Niemeyer commissioned to design Tripoli's International Fair
why: The site was never finished due to the 1975 war; UNESCO listed it in 2023.

title: Harissa cable car opens
why: Teleferique to the Our Lady shrine.

title: Palestinian fedayeen take Rashaya citadel
why: After the Battle of the Citadels; three people were executed at a checkpoint.

title: Upper galleries of Jeita inaugurated
why: Opened with a concert by composer Francois Bayle.

title: Sassine Square construction completed in Achrafieh
why: A central roundabout.

title: Israeli air raid on Ain al-Hilweh kills 11
why: Lebanese Army reports said 32 were wounded.

title: Former MP Maarouf Saad shot at Sidon fishermen protest
why: The protest against a fishing concession to Protéine foreshadowed the civil war; Saad was shot on 26 Feb 1975 and died on 6 March (corrected from 'MP'; he was a former MP).

title: Tripoli International Fair construction halted by war
why: Niemeyer's complex stayed unfinished for decades.

title: Baalbeck Festival suspended for the civil war
why: Activities ceased until 1997.

title: Union of Sidon and Zahrani Municipalities founded
why: Early federation of municipalities.

title: Jeita Grotto closes, tunnels used to store munitions
why: Closed during the civil war until 1995.

title: Operation Litani leaves Nabatieh 'hardly a house intact'
why: Israel's invasion drove the population out of the town.

title: Israeli air strike on Nahr al-Bared camp kills 4
why: Israel said it targeted a PFLP base; 25 were wounded.

title: Easter shelling of Sidon centre kills at least 16
why: SLA shelling of the city centre.

title: Israeli forces occupy Sidon for about two and a half years
why: Occupation from June 1982; Ain al-Hilweh was heavily bombed.

title: Marjayoun becomes SLA headquarters
why: The town hosted the South Lebanon Army until 2000.

title: Jezzine falls inside the Israeli security zone
why: Population later fell from 50,000 to about 3,000 by 1998 according to the cited article.

title: Iranian Revolutionary Guards set up in Baalbek's Sheikh Abdullah barracks
why: A base that fed the rise of Hezbollah.

title: Baalbek, Anjar, Byblos and Tyre inscribed as UNESCO sites
why: Lebanon's first four World Heritage listings.

title: Sana'a Mehaidli blows up Israeli convoy near Jezzine
why: A suicide attack killing two soldiers.

title: Tawheed and Arab Democratic Party militias clash in Tripoli
why: Roughly 150 killed and 200,000 displaced in the fighting, per the cited article.

title: Bomb damages Zahle Catholic cathedral complex
why: Damage to the cathedral compound.

title: SLA shells Nabatieh for three days, four killed
why: Eighteen were wounded.

title: Jounieh evacuation to Cyprus during Aoun war
why: 10,000 civilians left by sea.

title: Fatah defeats Abu Nidal group at Ain al-Hilweh
why: Three days of fighting killed 68.

title: Army attacks Palestinian positions around Sidon
why: Three days of fighting killed 73 per the cited article.

title: Ammunition dump explosion at Jounieh kills six
why: Thirty wounded.

title: Old Zahle Serail converted into a prison
why: Moved to Muallaqa in 2009.

title: Tripoli clock tower restored
why: Renovation by 1992; Palm Islands reserve also declared protected.

title: Marble clock mounted on Zahle cathedral tower
why: A local landmark.

title: Operation Accountability damages Nabatieh
why: Artillery and airstrikes from 25-31 July 1993.

title: Jeita Grotto reopens after the war
why: Reopened to the public.

title: Hezbollah car bomb destroys Israeli administrative HQ at Bint Jbeil
why: Followed by a bomb on 15 May killing six Israeli soldiers.

title: Baalbeck Festival returns in 1997 after civil-war pause
why: Official history: activities suspended 1975-1996 (22 years per the festival, about a quarter century per Wikipedia); resumed in 1997 (corrected from '22-year pause' in title).

title: Larnaca-Jounieh catamaran service starts
why: Sea link to Cyprus.

title: SLA shells Sidon, seven civilians killed
why: Hezbollah responded with 60-80 rockets.

title: Kadisha Valley and Cedars of God listed by UNESCO
why: Lebanon's fifth World Heritage listing.

title: Tyre Coast Nature Reserve decreed
why: A Ramsar site from 1999.

title: South Lebanon Army begins withdrawing from Jezzine
why: First pull-out from the occupied zone.

title: Gunmen kill three judges and a prosecutor in Sidon courthouse
why: Palais de Justice shooting.

title: Israeli air raids hit Baalbek, Al-Manar radio demolished
why: Two raids on 24-25 June.

title: Zahle Grand Hotel Kadri passes to the Catholic Church
why: Reopened in 2013 after 2011 closure.

title: Lebanese National Symphony Orchestra founded
why: Founded in Beirut.

title: Saida Municipal Stadium inaugurated
why: Built for the AFC Asian Cup 2000.

title: Patriarch Sfeir visits the Chouf and reconciles with Jumblatt
why: A landmark step in post-war mountain reconciliation.

title: Byblos International Festival founded
why: Held yearly in the old quarter.

title: Beirut Marathon begins
why: First edition of the annual marathon.

title: Souk el Tayeb farmers' market opens in Beirut
why: First farmers' market in the country.

title: Car bomb destroys radio station in Jounieh
why: Twenty-two wounded.

title: Syrian army leaves Tripoli after about three decades
why: The Syrian army stayed in the city until the 2005 withdrawal.

title: Jiyeh oil spill from war damage fouls Byblos harbour
why: Reported effect on the Jbeil coast.

title: Israeli forces take control of Marjayoun
why: On 11 Aug a 3,000-person convoy fled and was attacked near Hasbaya.

title: Tyre reading and cultural centre opens
why: Centre de Lecture et d'Animation Culturelle.

title: Army fights Fatah al-Islam at Nahr al-Bared
why: Battle ended 2 September; camp of 30,000 largely destroyed.

title: Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque completed in downtown Beirut
why: Built by Rafic Hariri's project.

title: Tripoli Special Economic Zone established
why: Tax exemptions for investment over $300,000.

title: Platinum Tower built in Beirut
why: A downtown high-rise.

title: Beirut Souks open in Solidere downtown
why: A 100,000 square metre retail centre.

title: Batroun International Festival born
why: Held each summer.

title: Beirut named World Book Capital by UNESCO
why: City-wide year-long programme.

title: Zahle prison moved to Muallaqa
why: Old Serail ceased to be a prison.

title: Zaitunay Bay opens in Beirut
why: Marina and promenade.

title: Byblos ranked second-best Middle East city by Conde Nast readers
why: A tourism ranking.

title: Wissam al-Hassan killed in Sassine Square bombing
why: Intelligence chief died in an Achrafieh car bomb.

title: IBC Enviro treatment plant opens at Sidon
why: Response to the waste crisis; a landfill mountain was later cleared.

title: Iranian embassy bombings in Beirut
why: Twin attacks.

title: Army builds concrete wall around Ain al-Hilweh
why: Wall with watchtowers completed 2016-17.

title: Byblos crowned 'Arab Tourism Capital'
why: Title by the Arab tourism ministers' union.

title: Jounieh named capital of Keserwan-Jbeil governorate
why: Governorate reorganisation.

title: Shakira performs at the Cedars festival
why: Cedars International Festival.

title: Bronze Age necropolis found at Byblos acropolis
why: Found on the southern acropolis.

title: Port blast damages Achrafieh, Bourj Hammoud, museums
why: The 2020 blast devastated these dense districts; Sursock Museum reopened in 2023, the National Museum in 2021.

title: Tyre port designated backup after Beirut explosion
why: Used as an alternative port.

title: Rachid Karami International Fair listed on UNESCO World Heritage and in danger
why: Niemeyer's unfinished fair in Tripoli.

title: Clashes at Ain al-Hilweh kill 11
why: July 30-31 fighting displaced 2,000.

title: Sursock Museum reopens
why: Reopened after restoration.

title: UNESCO enhanced protection for 34 Lebanese sites
why: Including Sidon, Byblos, Anjar, Baalbek.

title: Israeli strikes destroy Nabatieh's Ottoman-era market
why: Heritage damage.

title: Israeli strikes hit Nabatieh municipality meeting
why: At least 16 killed including the mayor.

title: Pope Leo XIV meets clergy at Harissa
why: During his Lebanon visit.

title: Nuhad es-Said Pavilion opens at National Museum
why: Second wing finally completed.

title: Illegal wedding held in Jeita Grotto triggers probe
why: Caves reopened 15 Nov.

title: Tyre's World Heritage site listed as endangered
why: Tyre was listed as endangered by UNESCO in 2026 following Israeli strikes.

title: Displacement orders empty Nabatieh despite ceasefire
why: City described as effectively empty.

title: Hezbollah rockets hit Orthodox church near Marjayoun
why: Saint George's church struck.
